Final summary:

I made two minimal changes to `semver.py` in the `createparser()` function to fix the CLI behavior:

1. **Line 643**: Changed `s = parser.add_subparsers()` to `s = parser.add_subparsers(dest="which", required=True)` - This makes a subcommand (compare or bump) mandatory. When `pysemver` is invoked without arguments, argparse now automatically raises `SystemExit` with code 2 instead of allowing the code to continue and crash with an `AttributeError`.

2. **Lines 662-664**: Changed `sb = parser_bump.add_subparsers(title="Bump commands", dest="bump")` to include `required=True` - This makes a bump type (major/minor/patch/prerelease/build) mandatory when using the bump subcommand. When `pysemver bump` is called without specifying which bump type, argparse now prints the help text for the bump subcommand and exits gracefully with code 2.

All 166 existing tests pass. The STATUS.json has been written at the repository root mapping R1 to probability 1.0.
